title: Manage Cast state and accepted current records
summary: Select or initialize private state, inspect or replace retained configuration, control sources, interpret current and legacy accounting, reconcile legacy employer ownership, and understand accepted current records.
use_when: Selected Cast state, retained configuration, source metadata, accounting or accepted current records must be understood or changed within the supported interface.
Older retained employer ownership needs the supported local reconciliation or state recovery limits must be understood.
do_not_use_when: Collection, exact public job-URL retrieval or data migration is required.
The intended result is program deployment, a provider credit purchase, credential replacement, destructive reset or downstream job selection.
outcome: Selected initialized private state, a locally verified complete configuration or source enrollment, or one transactionally reconciled retained ownership state.

interfaces.label: Clear a retained source enabled setting

effects: Initialization creates missing schema-two accepted current state and preserves existing schema-one discovery records and consumed budgets without migration or collection.
Configuration replacement updates retained settings without starting collection, resetting usage or purchasing provider credits.
Source controls retain source metadata and evidence; disabling clears its retained enabled setting without fetching remote sources.

Ownership reconciliation repairs older schema-one associations under one mutation lock and transaction, preserving IDs, usage, runs, coverage and cursors. In schema-two state it returns zero changes and preserves accepted employers, source operators and snapshot revision.
authority: Cast owns state schema, complete configuration validation, source enrollment, local counters and supported ownership reconciliation.
The caller chooses policy and accounts; providers own external balances and billing.
success: The selected state operation completes and supported reads confirm its intended local result.

Reconciliation returns moved_sources, moved_jobs, quarantined_jobs, renamed_candidates and cleared_shared_identities counts. Material changes in legacy state preserve identity and gain revisions; current state returns zero changes.
failure_and_recovery: Stop callers before ownership reconciliation. Program recovery preserves discovery state.
Preserve successful observations and conservative usage after collection failure. Do not erase state to clear budgets or hand-edit individual rows.
Program recovery leaves discovery state and configuration unchanged; an older program can reject newer configuration fields.
privacy: Private state, exports and diagnostics can contain search interests, locators, posting text and collection history.
Credentials remain outside saved configuration, database rows, arguments and logs.
does_not_authorize: A provider purchase, credential replacement, state deletion, scheduled activation, model job or downstream application workflow.

consumers.statement: The current user may select and initialize Cast state, inspect or replace collection configuration, control sources and invoke the supported ownership repair.

preconditions.statement: Select the intended private state directory. Except explicit initialization, operations require supported initialized state and valid inputs. Stop callers before ownership reconciliation.

inputs.statement: State defaults to ~/.local/share/cast and can be selected with --state-dir PATH or CAST_STATE_DIR. The CLI flag selects independently of environment. config set --file supplies a complete schema-one configuration; config show --json returns the current complete machine input.
automatic_excluded_ats accepts distinct ashby, greenhouse or lever names. It defaults to ["ashby"] when omitted; an explicit empty array removes ATS exclusions while retaining source enabled policy.

source add URL accepts an optional existing company ID for ordinary websites. Supported ATS sources reject that override and use canonical provider/tenant compatibility associations. This exported association does not establish the optional current source operator or any job employer. source disable selects one source ID.

outputs.statement: CLI state commands use readable diagnosis/configuration and short write receipts by default. Global --json selects the existing success JSON results. State commands return local readiness, complete configuration, source enrollment or ownership-repair counts. Repair counts describe the selected local transaction rather than external collection coverage. Operational errors exit 1: text on stderr by default, or schema-one ok:false with error.detail on stderr with --json. Syntax errors remain Clap text on stderr with exit 2. The status-snapshot --json protocol and native Rust APIs remain unchanged.

data_semantics.statement: Configuration retains query families, terms, intervals, adapter settings and request caps. No collector applies them in this release. Changes do not reset consumed allowance, buy credits or configure provider billing.

Schema-one budgets describe historical conservative request accounting. TheirStack total covers the retained lifetime rather than a provider monthly balance. Schema-two state has no request ledger or run history: usage is zero, last run is null and query coverage is empty. Cast does not collect or consume request allowance.

Schema-one reconciliation moves ATS associations to canonical provider/tenant companies, sets older or affected shared-host JSON-LD jobs to unknown, resets source collection status, restores affected candidate names and clears shared-host domains, website URLs and identity aliases. Schema-two reconciliation preserves accepted employer/operator associations without deriving either from the other.

cast::current defines Company, Job, Source, Location, JobLocation and JobSource plus SCHEMA for company, job, source, location, job_location and job_source. Employer and optional source operator are distinct company references; workplaces and work_mode are distinct. Both joins have composite primary keys, with one URL per job/source pair. The core holds one accepted current record per job; duplicates and conflicting source values require resolution before writing. The core has no history or collection mechanics.

Schema-two meta retains configuration, snapshot revision and company aliases; compatibility columns in company/job/source retain current export fields, including supplied timestamps, evidence, compensation, current entity revisions and source controls. There are no revision-history, observation, request-ledger or run tables. Cast accepted-record writes replace a job and its workplace/source links atomically and require schema-two state. Company/job first_seen_at and last_seen_at must be valid RFC 3339 values in order and normalize to UTC with nine fractional-second digits for chronological string comparison. Updates retain the first-seen instant and do not move the last-seen instant backwards. Existing location IDs retain their names. There is no CLI job ingestion interface.

identity_and_units.statement: The selected state directory identifies an independent Cast database named cast.sqlite3. Legacy paid accounting uses TheirStack credits, Brave requests, HTTP requests and elapsed seconds; daily and monthly windows use UTC.

Legacy repair preserves source/job IDs, paid usage, run history, coverage and cursors. Changed jobs and companies gain revisions, and each legacy repair invocation advances snapshot_revision. Schema-two reconciliation preserves all accepted records and the snapshot revision.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Configuration and doctor reads describe selected local state at invocation. Doctor checks configuration and credential presence; it does not establish provider authentication, balance or current posting availability.
Installed documentation, initialization and local diagnosis do not establish current provider allowance or successful collection.

access.statement: The current-user CLI is the state administration boundary. The state directory uses mode 0700 and cast.sqlite3 uses mode 0600. Configuration is stored in database metadata.
Direct SQLite reads and writes are not supported integration or repair surfaces.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Initialization creates database schema 2 when state is missing and preserves existing schema-one records and usage without migration. Store open supports both formats. Only one writer uses a selected directory, with a kernel-backed mutation lock. Legacy ownership reconciliation commits one transaction and makes no provider request.

Repeating legacy reconciliation leaves material records unchanged but advances snapshot_revision. Corrected legacy associations remain visible through reads. Current-state reconciliation reports no changes and preserves snapshot_revision.
Source disable retains records and clears the enabled setting. Ordinary website source add without a company ID creates or reuses a hostname candidate. Neither command retrieves remote records.

Missing state, including deployment setup, uses the accepted current model. Existing schema-one state remains supported without migration. Both storage formats retain the existing public read types and export schema 1; older programs that support only database schema 1 cannot open schema-two state.

operational_limits.statement: Retained configuration defaults are 200 total and 60 daily TheirStack credits, 1,000 monthly and 30 daily Brave requests, 500 HTTP requests per run, 3,000 daily HTTP requests, 600 seconds per run, 50 careers-source collections per run and 50 targeted adapter pages via max_verifications_per_run. No collector applies these limits in this release.
No automatic database migration, pruning, destructive reset or state uninstaller is provided.
No future migration, retention horizon, state-size bound or deprecation window is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Database, configuration, export, contract and release versions are distinct. Configuration schema remains 1 with automatic_excluded_ats. Older programs that reject unknown fields cannot read configuration written with that field. Program recovery restores no previous state or configuration.
No future database migration or deprecation window is promised.

reliances.statement: Supported record reads establish retained identities, revisions, attribution and post-repair evidence.
